predecessors.name: Germiyanids
predecessors.text: Birgi, Ephesus and the Maeander valley, held by Mehmed Bey, 'originally a vassal of the Germiyanids'

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the Aydinid lands, annexed by the Ottoman Empire in 1426 (infobox)

ledger.x: 1308: Mehmed Bey declares the independence of the Aydinid beylik at Birgi.
1317: the Aydinids begin the siege of Smyrna.
ledger.cp: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1329: the siege of Smyrna ends in Aydinid hands.
ledger.cp: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1329: Smyrna is held by the Aydinids.
ledger.cp: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1344: the crusader fleet takes the harbour fortress of Smyrna.

wars.name: Aydinid siege of Smyrna
wars.outcome: The Aydinids besiege Smyrna from 1317 to 1329 and hold it as a pirate base from 1326 to 1329.

wars.name: Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 (Aydinid intervention)
wars.outcome: The Aydinids under Umur 'participated in the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347'; the page names no territorial result.

wars.name: Smyrniote crusades
wars.outcome: The allied fleet beat the Turkish fleet at Pallene on 13 May 1344; the crusaders took the harbour fortress of Smyrna later in 1344 but not the acropolis; Umur Bey killed the patriarch and two leaders on 17 January 1345; a second crusade under Humbert II won…

wars.name: Bayezid I's conquest of Aydın, Saruhan and Menteshe
wars.outcome: Aydın is held by the Ottomans from 1390 to 1402; the Aydinids return under Timur's defeat of Bayezid at Ankara in 1402.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or a survey; the beylik's frontiers with Menteshe, Saruhan, Germiyan and the Byzantines are approximate throughout.
